## TRAPPIST-1: Largest Batch of Earth-sized Exoplanets

The most studied planetary system, aside from our own solar system, lies about 40 light-years away. We've looked at the seven rocky exoplanets orbiting the TRAPPIST-1 star with ground and space telescopes like Spitzer, Kepler, Hubble, and, now, the James Webb Space Telescope.

In March 2023, the first science from the Webb telescope was released. An analysis of TRAPPIST-1b, the innermost planet, revealed its dayside temperature and found little evidence of an [atmosphere](http://go.nasa.gov/42VAWiu).

In a press release on February 22, 2017, NASA announced the discovery of the most Earth-sized planets found in the habitable zone of a single star, called TRAPPIST-1. This system of seven rocky worlds–all of them with the potential for water on their surface – is an exciting discovery in the search for life on other worlds. There is the possibility that future study of this unique planetary system could reveal conditions suitable for life.

In February 2018, closer study of the seven planets suggested that some could harbor far more water than the oceans of Earth, in the form of atmospheric water vapor for the planets closest to their star, liquid water for others, and ice for those farthest away. The study pinned down the density of each planet more precisely, making TRAPPIST-1 the most thoroughly known planetary system apart from our own.

A 2021 study [revealed more](https://science.nasa.gov/universe/exoplanets/seven-rocky-trappist-1-planets-may-be-made-of-similar-stuff/) about TRAPPIST-1 planets. They are likely made of similar stuff, but they are different from Earth. That could mean they all contain about the same ratio of materials thought to compose most rocky planets, like iron, oxygen, magnesium, and silicon. But if this is the case, that ratio must be notably different than Earth's: The TRAPPIST-1 planets are about 8% less dense than they would be if they had the same makeup as our home planet.

## TRAPPIST-1: Largest Batch of Earth-sized Exoplanets

The most studied planetary system, aside from our own solar system, lies about 40 light-years away. We've looked at the seven rocky exoplanets orbiting the TRAPPIST-1 star with ground and space telescopes like Spitzer, Kepler, Hubble, and, now, the James Webb Space Telescope.

In March 2023, the first science from the Webb telescope was released. An analysis of TRAPPIST-1b, the innermost planet, revealed its dayside temperature and found little evidence of an [atmosphere](http://go.nasa.gov/42VAWiu).

In a press release on February 22, 2017, NASA announced the discovery of the most Earth-sized planets found in the habitable zone of a single star, called TRAPPIST-1. This system of seven rocky worlds–all of them with the potential for water on their surface – is an exciting discovery in the search for life on other worlds. There is the possibility that future study of this unique planetary system could reveal conditions suitable for life.

In February 2018, closer study of the seven planets suggested that some could harbor far more water than the oceans of Earth, in the form of atmospheric water vapor for the planets closest to their star, liquid water for others, and ice for those farthest away. The study pinned down the density of each planet more precisely, making TRAPPIST-1 the most thoroughly known planetary system apart from our own.

A 2021 study [revealed more](https://science.nasa.gov/universe/exoplanets/seven-rocky-trappist-1-planets-may-be-made-of-similar-stuff/) about TRAPPIST-1 planets. They are likely made of similar stuff, but they are different from Earth. That could mean they all contain about the same ratio of materials thought to compose most rocky planets, like iron, oxygen, magnesium, and silicon. But if this is the case, that ratio must be notably different than Earth's: The TRAPPIST-1 planets are about 8% less dense than they would be if they had the same makeup as our home planet.

# Exoplanet Catalog

This exoplanetary encyclopedia — continuously updated, with more than 6,000 entries — combines interactive 3D models and detailed data on all confirmed exoplanets. When you select a planet’s name, see a visualization of each world and system, along with vital statistics. Filter by exoplanet type, by discovery method, or by the mission or facility that found it.

![Image 39: An illustration shows a curved line of differently colored planets snaking out from a star in the background at the upper left.](https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/5k-exo-beauty-lores-final.png?w=1920)

## key to exoplanet types

[![Image 40](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/terrestrial.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)

### [Terrestrial](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)
A type of exoplanet made of rock or metal, smaller than Earth, possibly with oceans or atmospheres (artist's concept).

[![Image 41](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/superearth.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)

### [Super Earth](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)
Super-Earth exoplanets are also rocky, but between Earth and Neptune in size (artist's concept).

[![Image 42](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/neptunelike.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)

### [Neptune-like](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)
This variety of exoplanet is similar in size to Uranus and Neptune, with an atmosphere of mostly hydrogen or helium (artist's concept).

[![Image 43](https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/gasgiant.jpg?w=150&h=150&crop=1)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)

### [Gas Giant](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)
Gas Giant exoplanets are as massive as Saturn or Jupiter, or larger; this category also includes "hot Jupiters," which orbit close to their stars (artist's concept).

[![Image 44](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/unknown.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Unknown&content_list=true)

## **Do NASA Science and Explore Key Questions about the Universe**

*    01  ### **Exoplanet Watch**

NASA invites people of all ages and backgrounds to participate in authentic NASA research via "citizen science" or "participatory science" projects, where volunteers and amateurs have helped make thousands of important scientific discoveries. As a part of the Exoplanet Watch project, you'll help scientists track and study exoplanets as they transit in front of stars.

[Get Involved](https://science.nasa.gov/citizen-science/summary/exoplanet-watch/)   
*    02  ### UNITE

Do you have your own telescope? You can help observe newly discovered exoplanets and collect information about their transits to help characterize their orbits. UNITE participants coordinate with other citizen scientists and researchers around the globe to track and learn about these new worlds.

[Learn More](https://science.nasa.gov/citizen-science/summary/unite-unistellar-network-investigating-tess-exoplanets/)

# Exoplanet Catalog

This exoplanetary encyclopedia — continuously updated, with more than 6,000 entries — combines interactive 3D models and detailed data on all confirmed exoplanets. When you select a planet’s name, see a visualization of each world and system, along with vital statistics. Filter by exoplanet type, by discovery method, or by the mission or facility that found it.

![Image 39: An illustration shows a curved line of differently colored planets snaking out from a star in the background at the upper left.](https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/5k-exo-beauty-lores-final.png?w=1920)

## key to exoplanet types

[![Image 40](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/terrestrial.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)

### [Terrestrial](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)
A type of exoplanet made of rock or metal, smaller than Earth, possibly with oceans or atmospheres (artist's concept).

[![Image 41](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/superearth.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)

### [Super Earth](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)
Super-Earth exoplanets are also rocky, but between Earth and Neptune in size (artist's concept).

[![Image 42](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/neptunelike.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)

### [Neptune-like](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)
This variety of exoplanet is similar in size to Uranus and Neptune, with an atmosphere of mostly hydrogen or helium (artist's concept).

[![Image 43](https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/gasgiant.jpg?w=150&h=150&crop=1)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)

### [Gas Giant](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)
Gas Giant exoplanets are as massive as Saturn or Jupiter, or larger; this category also includes "hot Jupiters," which orbit close to their stars (artist's concept).

[![Image 44](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/unknown.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Unknown&content_list=true)

# Exoplanet Catalog

This exoplanetary encyclopedia — continuously updated, with more than 6,000 entries — combines interactive 3D models and detailed data on all confirmed exoplanets. When you select a planet’s name, see a visualization of each world and system, along with vital statistics. Filter by exoplanet type, by discovery method, or by the mission or facility that found it.

## key to exoplanet types

[![Image 39](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/terrestrial.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)

### [Terrestrial](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)
A type of exoplanet made of rock or metal, smaller than Earth, possibly with oceans or atmospheres (artist's concept).

[![Image 40](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/superearth.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)

### [Super Earth](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)
Super-Earth exoplanets are also rocky, but between Earth and Neptune in size (artist's concept).

[![Image 41](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/neptunelike.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)

### [Neptune-like](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)
This variety of exoplanet is similar in size to Uranus and Neptune, with an atmosphere of mostly hydrogen or helium (artist's concept).

[![Image 42](https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/gasgiant.jpg?w=150&h=150&crop=1)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)

### [Gas Giant](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)
Gas Giant exoplanets are as massive as Saturn or Jupiter, or larger; this category also includes "hot Jupiters," which orbit close to their stars (artist's concept).

[![Image 43](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/unknown.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Unknown&content_list=true)

## **Do NASA Science and Explore Key Questions about the Universe**

*    01  ### **Exoplanet Watch**

NASA invites people of all ages and backgrounds to participate in authentic NASA research via "citizen science" or "participatory science" projects, where volunteers and amateurs have helped make thousands of important scientific discoveries. As a part of the Exoplanet Watch project, you'll help scientists track and study exoplanets as they transit in front of stars.

[Get Involved](https://science.nasa.gov/citizen-science/summary/exoplanet-watch/)   
*    02  ### UNITE

Do you have your own telescope? You can help observe newly discovered exoplanets and collect information about their transits to help characterize their orbits. UNITE participants coordinate with other citizen scientists and researchers around the globe to track and learn about these new worlds.

# Exoplanet Catalog

This exoplanetary encyclopedia — continuously updated, with more than 6,000 entries — combines interactive 3D models and detailed data on all confirmed exoplanets. When you select a planet’s name, see a visualization of each world and system, along with vital statistics. Filter by exoplanet type, by discovery method, or by the mission or facility that found it.

## key to exoplanet types

[![Image 39](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/terrestrial.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)

### [Terrestrial](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)
A type of exoplanet made of rock or metal, smaller than Earth, possibly with oceans or atmospheres (artist's concept).

[![Image 40](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/superearth.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)

### [Super Earth](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)
Super-Earth exoplanets are also rocky, but between Earth and Neptune in size (artist's concept).

[![Image 41](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/neptunelike.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)

### [Neptune-like](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)
This variety of exoplanet is similar in size to Uranus and Neptune, with an atmosphere of mostly hydrogen or helium (artist's concept).

[![Image 42](https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/gasgiant.jpg?w=150&h=150&crop=1)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)

### [Gas Giant](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)
Gas Giant exoplanets are as massive as Saturn or Jupiter, or larger; this category also includes "hot Jupiters," which orbit close to their stars (artist's concept).

[![Image 43](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/unknown.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Unknown&content_list=true)

# Exoplanet Catalog

This exoplanetary encyclopedia — continuously updated, with more than 6,000 entries — combines interactive 3D models and detailed data on all confirmed exoplanets. When you select a planet’s name, see a visualization of each world and system, along with vital statistics. Filter by exoplanet type, by discovery method, or by the mission or facility that found it.

## key to exoplanet types

[![Image 39](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/terrestrial.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)

### [Terrestrial](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)
A type of exoplanet made of rock or metal, smaller than Earth, possibly with oceans or atmospheres (artist's concept).

[![Image 40](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/superearth.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)

### [Super Earth](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)
Super-Earth exoplanets are also rocky, but between Earth and Neptune in size (artist's concept).

[![Image 41](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/neptunelike.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)

### [Neptune-like](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)
This variety of exoplanet is similar in size to Uranus and Neptune, with an atmosphere of mostly hydrogen or helium (artist's concept).

[![Image 42](https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/gasgiant.jpg?w=150&h=150&crop=1)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)

### [Gas Giant](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)
Gas Giant exoplanets are as massive as Saturn or Jupiter, or larger; this category also includes "hot Jupiters," which orbit close to their stars (artist's concept).

[![Image 43](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/unknown.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Unknown&content_list=true)

## **Do NASA Science and Explore Key Questions about the Universe**

*    01  ### **Exoplanet Watch**

NASA invites people of all ages and backgrounds to participate in authentic NASA research via "citizen science" or "participatory science" projects, where volunteers and amateurs have helped make thousands of important scientific discoveries. As a part of the Exoplanet Watch project, you'll help scientists track and study exoplanets as they transit in front of stars.

[Get Involved](https://science.nasa.gov/citizen-science/summary/exoplanet-watch/)   
*    02  ### UNITE

Do you have your own telescope? You can help observe newly discovered exoplanets and collect information about their transits to help characterize their orbits. UNITE participants coordinate with other citizen scientists and researchers around the globe to track and learn about these new worlds.

[Learn More](https://science.nasa.gov/citizen-science/summary/unite-unistellar-network-investigating-tess-exoplanets/)

# Exoplanet Catalog

This exoplanetary encyclopedia — continuously updated, with more than 6,000 entries — combines interactive 3D models and detailed data on all confirmed exoplanets. When you select a planet’s name, see a visualization of each world and system, along with vital statistics. Filter by exoplanet type, by discovery method, or by the mission or facility that found it.

![Image 38: An illustration shows a curved line of differently colored planets snaking out from a star in the background at the upper left.](https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/5k-exo-beauty-lores-final.png?w=1920)

## key to exoplanet types

[![Image 39](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/terrestrial.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)

### [Terrestrial](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)
A type of exoplanet made of rock or metal, smaller than Earth, possibly with oceans or atmospheres (artist's concept).

[![Image 40](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/superearth.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)

### [Super Earth](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)
Super-Earth exoplanets are also rocky, but between Earth and Neptune in size (artist's concept).

[![Image 41](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/neptunelike.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)

### [Neptune-like](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)
This variety of exoplanet is similar in size to Uranus and Neptune, with an atmosphere of mostly hydrogen or helium (artist's concept).

[![Image 42](https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/gasgiant.jpg?w=150&h=150&crop=1)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)

### [Gas Giant](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)
Gas Giant exoplanets are as massive as Saturn or Jupiter, or larger; this category also includes "hot Jupiters," which orbit close to their stars (artist's concept).

[![Image 43](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/unknown.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Unknown&content_list=true)

# Exoplanet Catalog

This exoplanetary encyclopedia — continuously updated, with more than 6,000 entries — combines interactive 3D models and detailed data on all confirmed exoplanets. When you select a planet’s name, see a visualization of each world and system, along with vital statistics. Filter by exoplanet type, by discovery method, or by the mission or facility that found it.

## key to exoplanet types

[![Image 39](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/terrestrial.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)

### [Terrestrial](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)
A type of exoplanet made of rock or metal, smaller than Earth, possibly with oceans or atmospheres (artist's concept).

[![Image 40](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/superearth.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)

### [Super Earth](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)
Super-Earth exoplanets are also rocky, but between Earth and Neptune in size (artist's concept).

[![Image 41](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/neptunelike.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)

### [Neptune-like](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)
This variety of exoplanet is similar in size to Uranus and Neptune, with an atmosphere of mostly hydrogen or helium (artist's concept).

[![Image 42](https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/gasgiant.jpg?w=150&h=150&crop=1)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)

### [Gas Giant](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)
Gas Giant exoplanets are as massive as Saturn or Jupiter, or larger; this category also includes "hot Jupiters," which orbit close to their stars (artist's concept).

[![Image 43](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/unknown.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Unknown&content_list=true)

NASA invites people of all ages and backgrounds to participate in authentic NASA research via "citizen science" or "participatory science" projects, where volunteers and amateurs have helped make thousands of important scientific discoveries. [Get Involved](https://science.nasa.gov/citizen-science/summary/exoplanet-watch/)   
*    02  ### UNITE

Do you have your own telescope? You can help observe newly discovered exoplanets and collect information about their transits to help characterize their orbits. UNITE participants coordinate with other citizen scientists and researchers around the globe to track and learn about these new worlds.

# Exoplanet Catalog

This exoplanetary encyclopedia — continuously updated, with more than 6,000 entries — combines interactive 3D models and detailed data on all confirmed exoplanets. When you select a planet’s name, see a visualization of each world and system, along with vital statistics. Filter by exoplanet type, by discovery method, or by the mission or facility that found it.

## key to exoplanet types

[![Image 39](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/terrestrial.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)

### [Terrestrial](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Terrestrial&content_list=true)
A type of exoplanet made of rock or metal, smaller than Earth, possibly with oceans or atmospheres (artist's concept).

[![Image 40](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/superearth.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)

### [Super Earth](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Super+Earth&content_list=true)
Super-Earth exoplanets are also rocky, but between Earth and Neptune in size (artist's concept).

[![Image 41](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/neptunelike.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)

### [Neptune-like](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Neptune-like&content_list=true)
This variety of exoplanet is similar in size to Uranus and Neptune, with an atmosphere of mostly hydrogen or helium (artist's concept).

[![Image 42](https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/gasgiant.jpg?w=150&h=150&crop=1)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)

### [Gas Giant](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Gas+Giant&content_list=true)
Gas Giant exoplanets are as massive as Saturn or Jupiter, or larger; this category also includes "hot Jupiters," which orbit close to their stars (artist's concept).

[![Image 43](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/astro/exo-explore/assets/content/planets/unknown.jpg?w=1280&h=720&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/exoplanet-catalog/?planet_type=Unknown&content_list=true)
